valuation_philosophy: Genesis is a Crown-controlled (51%), NZX50-liquid integrated gentailer whose thesis is income (6.4% gross imputed yield) plus a funded but capital-intensive growth programme (~$2bn Gen35 pipeline to FY32), NOT a growth-multiple story. FY26 guidance was upgraded twice (to $515-545m normalised EBITDAF, 23-Apr-2026) on a genuine mix of structural margin gains (retail netback, HFO contracting) and favourable hydrology that will not repeat every year -- the DCF anchors Y1 (FY26) to the guided $530m midpoint but reverts Y2 (FY27) toward mid-cycle before resuming structural growth into the FY28 guidance and FY32 $650-750m outlook. Reported free cash flow is deliberately modelled as suppressed for several years by SIB capex ($130-140m/yr) plus ~$2bn of growth capex concentrated FY26-32 -- this is exactly why the Feb-2026 $400m equity raise happened, and the DCF should not paper over it with a flat margin. The stock trades at NZ$2.63, at the top of its 52-week range and implying ~8.9x EV/FY26F EBITDAF and ~1.02x P/B -- both squarely inside GNE's own 8.1-13.6x / 0.83-1.73x historical trading bands (Step 8c check below), i.e. the market is pricing GNE fairly against its own history, not irrationally. Against that backdrop this DCF's base case comes out BELOW the current price ($1.53, -41.8%) -- the capex programme genuinely depresses discounted cash flow for years before the FY32 payoff arrives, and a buyer at $2.63 is relying on execution of a large, multi-year capital programme (plus continued benign hydrology) that is not yet in the cash flows. The bull case ($2.67, +1.4%) requires the pipeline to deliver on schedule and capital-efficiently with benign hydrology and regulation. The bear case ($0.615, -76.6%) models a RATIONAL response to disappointing returns -- management curtails discretionary growth capex to 47% of the base case rather than funding the full pipeline regardless of payoff -- and still shows a severe drawdown once the higher 10.5% WACC, weaker terminal EBITDAF ($533m vs $740m) and a largely fixed NZ$1,300m net debt load are applied against a smaller enterprise value. Probability-weighted IV across Bull/Base/Bear (25/50/25) is $1.59, still below the current price. A modest-to-negative DCF upside is the honest conclusion here, not a modelling error -- it is consistent with GNE being priced as a bond-proxy income stock near cyclical highs rather than a statistically cheap value opportunity, and the range across scenarios ($0.615 to $2.67) illustrates genuinely asymmetric downside risk around a capex programme that has real optionality to be curtailed if it disappoints, but whose success is not yet reflected in current cash flows at any scenario weighting.

inputs.shares_outstanding_note: CSV's latest SharesOutstanding (1,110.4m, 31-Dec-2025) is PRE the Feb-2026 NZ$400m equity raise (NZ$300m 1-for-7.9 rights offer at $2.05 -> 146.3m shares + NZ$100m placement -> 46.5m shares, settled Mar-2026). Using the pre-raise count would overstate per-share value by ~17%. This model uses 1,303.2m as the current/base share count.
inputs.net_debt_source: Reported net debt at 31-Dec-2025 was NZ$1,315.0m (drawn borrowings less cash less fair-value adjustments of $78.7m, per H1 FY26 presentation). The Feb-2026 $400m raise funds the Gen35 growth capex programme, not debt repayment, so it is NOT simply subtracted from net debt. Pro-forma net debt is assumed at NZ$1,300m, reflecting modest near-term paydown ahead of capex ramping through FY27-32; leverage target is 2.2-2.6x Net Debt/EBITDAF.
inputs.interest_income_note: Genesis holds net DEBT, not net cash (finance revenue is trivial, $2.8m FY25) -- no interest-income double-count to strip.
inputs.sbc_source: GNE.NZ FY2025 Annual Report note G1 (Share-based payments), $0.9m reported FY25; verified immaterial (~0.02-0.03% of revenue) across FY2020-2026.
inputs.uncovered_dilution_note: SBC is immaterial (~$0.9m/yr vs ~$500m EBITDAF) so no SBC-driven dilution adjustment is material. Genesis runs a Dividend Reinvestment Plan (DRP, ~$40m/yr of new shares at recent prices) and has NO buyback programme; share count is grown ~0.75%/yr in projections to reflect ongoing DRP issuance.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGR is unusable as a DCF driver: reported NPAT/EPS is heavily distorted by unrealised derivative fair-value movements and generation-asset revaluations (3yr EPS CAGR -10.0% vs 5yr +28.2% -- pure noise, not earnings power). EBITDAF CAGR is also low/volatile (1-5%) because EBITDAF swings 11-22% of revenue year to year on hydrology and wholesale prices; the 8-year mean EBITDAF ($407.8m) sits well below FY26 guidance ($530m midpoint). Equity/book-value CAGR (7.5-7.7%) is the most stable historical anchor and is broadly consistent with revenue CAGR (7.2-8.9%), so it is used as the reference historical growth rate -- though the DCF itself is built bottom-up from EBITDAF guidance/outlook and a component capex/tax/D&A build, not by extrapolating this CAGR directly, given GNE's own guidance framework is EBITDAF-dollars, not a revenue-margin model.
historical_growth.notes: Owner (SBC-adjusted) FCF CAGRs are barely different from reported (SBC is immaterial, ~$0.4-0.9m/yr). Reported FCF CAGR itself is NEGATIVE over both 3yr and 5yr windows (capex step-up outpacing OCF growth), consistent with the capex-suppression thesis used in the projections.

assumptions.modelling_approach: EBITDAF-anchored component build, NOT a flat FCF-margin or revenue-margin extrapolation. Revenue is extremely noisy at GNE (wholesale fuel/purchase costs pass through revenue without moving EBITDAF dollars -- historical revenue YoY swung -16.2% to +28.4%, and H1 FY26 revenue FELL 12.9% YoY even as normalised EBITDAF rose 38%). Revenue is therefore projected only as a smoothed reference series (4%/yr base case) used for D&A%, SBC% and working-capital-on-growth calculations, while EBITDAF itself is projected directly off management's own guidance markers: FY26 guided $515-545m (midpoint $530m used as Y1, reflecting a real hydrology/margin tailwind); FY27 reverts toward mid-cycle ($490m, still above the $407.8m 8yr historical mean, reflecting banked structural gains from HFO contracting and netback improvement); FY28 approaches the guided 'mid-to-upper $500m' target; FY32 reaches the guided $650-750m outlook midpoint; FY33-35 decelerate toward the 2.25% terminal growth rate as the Gen35 capex programme completes.

bull.narrative: Hydrology stays favourable, Gen35 solar/BESS/HFO delivery on or ahead of schedule and capital-efficient, FY32 outlook upper end ($830m by FY35) achieved, regulatory review outcome benign.

bear.narrative: Dry-year reversion is sharp (FY27 EBITDAF troughs at $425m) and the Energy Competition Task Force non-discrimination rules plus continued Kupe decline keep margins structurally weaker than base for the full decade -- Y10 EBITDAF reaches only $533m, 28% below base's $740m. Critically, this scenario assumes RATIONAL management: when early returns on the Gen35 pipeline disappoint, the board stage-gates and curtails the DISCRETIONARY portion of growth capex rather than continuing to fund a programme that is not paying off. Only the already-committed ~236MW (~$371m), the in-flight Huntly BESS Stage 1, and a partial Leeston/Edgecumbe solar tranche are completed (front-loaded FY26-28); everything beyond that is deferred or cancelled from FY29 onward as new FIDs stop being approved. Total growth capex is $1,020m over 10 years (47% of the base case's $2,170m). SIB capex stays at $140m/yr (non-discretionary, cannot be deferred without risking plant/network reliability).

bear.note: Positive equity value throughout (no artefact of unfunded capex against a flat EBITDAF), reflecting a coherent 'rational management curtails growth capex when returns disappoint' bear case rather than 'company funds the full $2bn programme for near-zero return.' Terminal value is Gordon-bound (not the EV/EBITDAF cap) because at a 10.5% WACC / 1.75% terminal growth the implied Gordon FCF multiple (~11.6x) sits below the 7.0x EV/EBITDAF cap once converted using this scenario's Y10 FCF/EBITDAF conversion ratio (54.6%, similar to base case's 54.0% -- i.e. NOT assuming worse cash conversion than base, only a lower absolute EBITDAF level and a higher discount rate). See bear_case_construction for why growth capex was cut and how the resulting IV compares with an initial ballpark expectation.

sensitivity.note: Matrix built on base-case owner FCF/EBITDAF path with the 8.0x EV/EBITDAF terminal cap held fixed; at WACC<=8% the cap binds across the full terminal-growth range (values are flat by row), which is the cap doing its job of preventing Gordon-growth blow-up.

historical_multiples.note: FY-end (30-Jun) share prices supplied for FY2018-FY2026; FY2026 uses current price 2.59-2.63 and GUIDED (not yet actual) EBITDAF/shares.

historical_range.pe: 12.5-123.2x (NPAT distorted by FV items -- not meaningful)

current_implied_multiples_at_2.63.note: Both sit squarely inside GNE's own historical trading bands -- the market is pricing GNE consistently with its own history at $2.63, not irrationally.

dcf_implied_multiples_at_base_iv.diagnosis: Base-case DCF IV of $1.53 implies ~6.2x EV/FY26F EBITDAF and ~0.59x P/B -- BELOW even the low end of GNE's own 8.1-13.6x EV/EBITDAF and 0.83-1.73x P/B historical trading history. Per Step 8c.4/8c.5 this was investigated: (a) the terminal cap (8.0x, at the historical floor) is appropriate as a CEILING and is not the main driver -- Gordon growth (6,057.7) and the cap (5,920.0) are close together, so the cap is barely binding, not artificially suppressing value; (b) growth capex assumptions ($1,910m over FY26-32) match the disclosed ~$2bn Gen35 pipeline, not an overstated figure; (c) sensitivity shows IV reaches only $1.75-1.99 even at a generous 7-8% WACC with a 8-9x cap -- still below $2.63. The gap is genuine: the DCF explicit period (949m of 10yr PV FCF) is heavily suppressed by ~$2.3-2.8bn of combined SIB and growth capex over FY26-32, which is the entire point of the Feb-2026 equity raise and the FY32 EBITDAF step-up thesis. The conclusion is not a modelling artefact to be 'fixed' -- it means a buyer at $2.63 (~8.9x EV/EBITDAF, in-line with history) is paying a price that already assumes the ~$2bn capex programme converts smoothly into the FY32 $650-750m EBITDAF outlook, with limited further margin of safety, and it is not statistically cheap on a explicit discounted-cash-flow view even though it is fairly priced on trailing multiples.

sanity_check.bear_case_note: The rebuilt bear case ($0.615/share, -76.6%) is internally consistent -- positive equity value, growth capex curtailed to 47% of the base case in response to disappointing early returns (a FID-gating decision Genesis's own pipeline structure supports), and EBITDAF still shows a genuine (if weak) lift from the capital that IS retained. It replaces an earlier version that spent MORE capex than the base case for near-zero EBITDAF growth and produced an economically meaningless negative equity value -- see bear_case_construction for the full before/after reasoning.

bear_case_construction.problem_with_prior_version: The original bear case spent $2,530m of growth capex over 10 years (MORE than the base case's $2,170m) while growing EBITDAF only from $500m to $510m -- a ~0.4% return on that capital versus ~9.7% in the base case. That is not a rational-agent scenario: no board funds a $2.5bn programme for a decade at a 0.4% return, and Genesis's own pipeline is explicitly FID-gated (e.g. Leeston FID targeted Q1 FY27, Rangiriri pre-FID), meaning the spend is optional and would be curtailed long before a decade of near-zero payoff. It also produced a negative intrinsic value (-$0.38/share), which is not a meaningful output for a BBB+-rated, Crown-controlled utility with a ~NZ$500m EBITDAF base and a liquid NZX50 listing -- equity here is bounded well above zero.
bear_case_construction.fix_applied: Growth capex is curtailed to reflect a rational board: only the already-committed ~236MW (~$371m), the in-flight Huntly BESS Stage 1, and a partial early-stage solar tranche are completed (front-loaded FY26-28, consistent with committed spend that cannot be unwound), then new FID approvals stop from ~FY29 onward once early returns disappoint. Total growth capex falls to $1,020m over 10 years (47% of the base case's $2,170m). SIB capex is held at the non-discretionary $140m/yr. The EBITDAF path is correspondingly rebuilt to reflect a genuine but weak lift from the retained capital (troughs at $425m in FY27, recovers only to $533m by FY35 -- 28% below the base case's $740m), rather than assuming the curtailed spend delivers nothing. WACC (10.5%) and terminal growth (1.75%) are kept unchanged as legitimate risk premia for a dry-year/regulatory/Kupe-decline scenario; net debt (NZ$1,300m) is kept as the current-date snapshot used consistently across all three scenarios (this is a standard DCF enterprise-value bridge using today's balance sheet, not a projected decade-forward debt balance, so it does not need to move with the capex path).
bear_case_construction.result_vs_initial_expectation: The corrected mechanics produce intrinsic value of $0.615/share, a 76.6% drawdown from the $2.63 current price -- more severe than an initial ballpark expectation of ~$0.90-1.40 (45-65% drawdown). This was investigated rather than forced: pushing the bear EBITDAF path or FCF conversion any higher to land inside that range would require either (a) a Y10 EBITDAF within ~15% of the base case's $740m, or (b) Y10 FCF/EBITDAF conversion better than the base case's -- neither is a coherent 'poor outcome' story once growth capex has genuinely been cut to ~47% of base. The severity instead comes from three structurally fixed pieces that were correctly held constant per the brief: the 10.5% WACC (vs base 9.0%) compounds over a 10-year horizon, the Gordon terminal multiple this implies (~11.6x FCF) is materially below the base case's effective ~14.8x, and NZ$1,300m of net debt is a much larger fraction of a smaller enterprise value (60% of EV here vs 38% in base). The scenario is internally consistent (positive equity throughout, capex broadly proportionate to the EBITDAF delivered, no capex/debt mismatch) even though the resulting drawdown is deeper than the initial ballpark -- this is reported transparently rather than adjusted to hit a target range.
